questions.problem: If $\overset{―}{P}=\{a,b,c,d,e,f\}$ and $\overset{―}{Q}=\{a,c,e\},$ then what is $\overset{―}{P\cup Q}?$
questions.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for unions states that

$$
\overset{―}{P\cup Q}≡\overset{―}{P}\cap \overset{―}{Q}.
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{P\cup Q} & =\overset{―}{P}\cap \overset{―}{Q} \\  & =\{a,b,c,d,e,f\}\cap \{a,c,e\} \\  & =\{a,c,e\}.\end{aligned}
$$
